title: Add repetition_penalty to OpenAI API compatible generation endpoints.
body:
I will open a PR for this soon if no one else beats me to it. However, with the advent of simply needing more control and customization from the API, would it make sense to a) make a general API in a new API file and have OpenAI proxy that file or b) keep expanding the OpenAI compatible API with extras that don't break using it as an OpenAI API?

I think a) is better, but takes a lot longer to do. I'd like to avoid holding back development of the API and thus apps built on the API if we can help it.

Addressed in #1536

linked_prs.title: Update OpenAI API and begin diverging.
linked_prs.body:
## Why are these changes needed?

Under normal production conditions, the token check API call is likely to be called multiple times in order to get the token lengths of the segments of a prompt (e.g. prompt, history, preprompt, etc.), this causes unnecessary overhead in the way of making multiple HTTP requests one after another. 

* This PR causes the format and endpoint of "token_check" to be changed (this is a breaking change, but hopefully doing it early allows for it to be used in the better way instead of making two API endpoints for this) where one can submit an array of prompts for validation.
* This PR adds a new endpoint for chat completions that are not compliant to the OpenAI API spec. (Closes #1537)
* This PR begins diverging the two APIs in the code without doing a ton of work to separate them upfront.

ai_judgment.response: Yes. This issue involves adding a parameter (`repetition_penalty`) to OpenAI API-compatible endpoints, which ties to LLM provider usage and SDK parameters. It aligns with the criteria for agent issues as it concerns LLM operation and customization.
